title: Use movement-linked scenarios instead of treating movement as off-limits
summary: Movement is inseparable from aim in FPS games, and aim trainers can still isolate useful movement-linked practice through strafe, dodge, and anti-movement scenario types.
why: Aim quality in games depends on responding while your own position is changing.
Trainer movement scenarios can isolate that adaptation even if they do not replace full live duel movement.
actions: Add at least one strafe or dodge drill if your aim falls apart while moving.
Use anti-movement drills to get comfortable adjusting onto targets while your position shifts automatically.
Treat these drills as isolation work, then validate them in actual game fights later.
avoid: Do not assume movement can only be trained in real matches and nowhere else.

drills.label: Movement strafe / anti-movement block
drills.reason: These scenario types isolate aim while position is changing, which many routines undertrain.

evidence.claim: Strafe, dodge, and anti-movement scenarios can provide viable isolated practice for aiming while moving.
evidence.excerpt: Training movement in the aim trainer is in fact possible and viable.
